links.comparator_used: Single-modality models: image-only vision models and language-only classifiers, compared with VLMs using image plus text
links.outcome: Maxillary sinus normal/abnormal classification AUC by input modality and label source
links.effect: On raw ChatGPT labels (n=300), language models reached AUC 0·992 to 1·000, vision models 0·799 to 0·880, and VLM image-only probes 0·63 to 0·69. On radiologist-confirmed labels (n=297), language and text-derived VLM performance fell (BERT-base AUC 0·999 to 0·837), while vision performance was stable or improved (DenseNet-121 0·867 to 0·891).
links.tradeoff: The text advantage reflects alignment with self-generated labels, not verified diagnostic content. A meaningful share of raw ChatGPT text was clinically uninterpretable or unsupported by the imaging, and the radiologist reclassified 62 of 297 cases (21%).
links.quote: We show that raw, unverified ChatGPT-generated text produces the highest classification performance of any modality evaluated (AUC up to 1·000), exceeding image-only and image-plus-text models—but that a meaningful proportion of this raw text is clinically uninterpretable, and that its apparent advantage collapses substantially once evaluated against a radiologist-confirmed reference standard on the same cases.

design_hint: radiologist verification of AI-generated text and labels
